Diversity is a whole lot more than what we look like or where we come from, it’s how we think and who we are. We welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. But we’re not doing it single-handily: Our Kyndryl Inclusion Networks are only one of many ways we create a workplace where all Kyndryls can find and provide support and advice. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you – and everyone next to you – the ability to bring your whole self to work, individually and collectively, and support the activation of our equitable culture. That’s the Kyndryl Way.

**What You Can Expect**

With state-of-the-art resources and Fortune 100 clients, every day is an opportunity to innovate, build new capabilities, new relationships, new processes, and new value. Kyndryl cares about your well-being and prides itself on offering benefits that give you choice, reflect the diversity of our employees and support you and your family through the moments that matter – wherever you are in your life journey. Our employee learning programs give you access to the best learning in the industry to receive certifications, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Skillsoft, and many more. Through our company-wide volunteering and giving platform, you can donate, start fundraisers, volunteer, and search over 2 million non-profit organizations. At Kyndryl, we invest heavily in you, we want you to succeed so that together, we will all succeed.

**Get Referred!**  
If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

title: Director of Design Execution
description:
### **About Switch**

At Switch, we don't just design, build and operate data centers—we are enabling the technology of the future. Led by Founder & CEO, Rob Roy, we believe in revolutionary innovation, operational excellence and the principle of karma. Switch is where talented people come together to EVOLVE the digital world.

We believe that innovation isn't just about technology—it's about the people, culture, and purpose that make it happen. Every Switch team member contributes to a mission greater than themselves: to create the world's most advanced digital infrastructure that powers the progress of humanity.

**The Role: Director of Design Execution**
------------------------------------------

The Director of Design Execution provides enterprise leadership for the practical execution, technical coordination, and field validation of data center designs across Switch's project portfolio. This role leads the team responsible for translating design intent into solutions that are safe, constructible, commissionable, operable, maintainable, and repeatable.

You will lead Design Execution from post-design handoff through construction, commissioning, turnover, and operational readiness while providing technical support throughout the infrastructure lifecycle. You will establish engineering governance, execution standards, decision and escalation processes, and feedback mechanisms that improve reliability and consistency across regions.

This role leads a team of technical subject matter experts and manages supporting third-party consultants and contractors. You will also partner closely with Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, EHS, Finance, Legal, and other stakeholders to improve project delivery and turn field experience into standards and lessons learned for future projects.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead and develop the Design Execution team, including technical subject matter experts and supporting third-party consultants and contractors.
* Set team priorities, allocate resources, establish performance expectations, and provide coaching and development.
* Lead Design Execution activities across the project lifecycle, including design handoff, construction, commissioning, turnover, operations support, infrastructure improvements, and end-of-life planning.
* Establish and maintain the engineering governance framework for post-IFC execution, including handoff requirements, engineering decision management, escalation pathways, design-change oversight, performance metrics, and continuous improvement.
* Translate design intent into practical field execution requirements that support constructability, commissioning, maintainability, and operational readiness.
* Oversee resolution of construction and field engineering issues, including complex procedure reviews, critical equipment concerns, and technical event support.
* Oversee engineering solutions for upgrades and retrofits that increase capacity, availability, efficiency, reliability, or operational capability across existing data centers.
* Provide technical leadership for electrical and mechanical infrastructure, including transformers, generators, UPS systems, power distribution, HVAC and cooling systems, controls, and related critical infrastructure.
* Review and interpret construction drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, sequences of operation, specifications, submittals, and other engineering documentation.
* Partner with Design Engineering to translate field experience, operational feedback, commissioning results, and lessons learned into improved standards and future designs.
* Coordinate with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, EHS, and other stakeholders to maintain consistent technical and execution standards across projects.
* Manage engineering consultants, vendors, contractors, and other external technical resources supporting Design Execution.
* Establish processes, procedures, and tools that enable consistent execution and support customer and project requirements across data center campuses.
* Establish and monitor Design Execution performance metrics and provide project, risk, and program updates to senior leadership.
* Lead assigned engineering projects and programs and ensure delivery against schedule, budget, quality, and operational requirements.
* Coordinate maintenance windows and implementation activities with facility leadership to minimize operational disruption.
* Ensure Design Execution activities comply with applicable codes, regulations, Switch requirements, and safety standards, including NFPA 70E requirements where applicable.
* Support Operations during turnover, customer-impacting events, near misses, and other complex technical situations.
* Identify systemic issues, recurring field challenges, and opportunities to improve execution, reliability, efficiency, and cost.
* Build strong working relationships across Operations, Finance, Legal, Construction, Commissioning, Design Engineering, and other stakeholders.
* Maintain an active field presence to understand conditions firsthand and validate that solutions can be executed as intended.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* You lead technical teams with clear expectations, accountability, coaching, and consistent follow-through.
* You make sound engineering decisions while balancing safety, reliability, constructability, cost, schedule, and operational impact.
* You can make informed recommendations when technical information is incomplete or conditions are changing.
* You identify design and execution risks early and develop practical solutions before they affect project or operational outcomes.
* You communicate complex engineering issues clearly to technical teams, business partners, and senior leadership.
* You build alignment across Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and external partners.
* You establish standards and governance that improve consistency without creating unnecessary barriers to execution.
* You use field experience, data, root cause analysis, and lessons learned to drive continuous improvement.
* You develop internal talent while holding consultants, contractors, and other external resources accountable for quality and results.
* You are comfortable spending time in the field to understand problems firsthand and validate solutions.
* You demonstrate the judgment, accountability, collaboration, and leadership expected under Switch's Culture Codes.

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive engineering experience supporting industrial, commercial, or mission-critical facilities such as data centers, power generation, or oil and gas facilities.
* 5+ years of experience leading engineering teams, technical professionals, consultants, or comparable resources.
* 4+ years of project management experience supporting data center engineering or comparable mission-critical infrastructure.
* Deep understanding of electrical and mechanical systems used in mission-critical environments, including power distribution, transformers, generators, switchgear, UPS systems, cooling systems, HVAC, controls, and fire protection.
* Experience leading or supporting construction, commissioning, turnover, operational readiness, retrofit, or infrastructure improvement activities.
* Experience managing engineering projects, consultants, contractors, and other external technical resources.
* Experience reading, interpreting, and reviewing construction drawings, specifications, submittals, wiring diagrams, schematics, sequences of operation, and MEP documentation.
* Experience with EPMS, SCADA, BMS, or comparable monitoring and controls systems.
* Strong knowledge of safety requirements and applicable OSHA standards for multi-megawatt or mission-critical facilities.
* Working knowledge of NFPA 70E and electrical safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to develop and execute solutions for complex engineering and operational problems.
* Strong project and program management, prioritization, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
* Experience using engineering, project management, calculation, data analysis, and collaboration tools.
* Ability to support after-hours or weekend activities when required for critical projects, maintenance windows, commissioning, or operational events.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as business needs require.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
* Professional Engineer registration or other relevant professional engineering certification.
* Experience leading enterprise or multi-region engineering programs within data centers or other mission-critical environments.
* Experience establishing engineering governance, technical standards, design-change processes, or post-IFC execution frameworks.
* Experience supporting root cause analysis, fleet optimization, lifecycle management, and infrastructure reliability programs.

We recognize that qualified candidates may not meet every preferred qualification. If your experience aligns with the core responsibilities of the role, we encourage you to apply.

### **Why Switch?**

* A Culture of Karma – We are self-motivated by karma, ensuring our actions contribute to a positive, supportive and forward-thinking environment.
* Industry Leading Designs – Work with the most advanced data center technology on the planet and be a part of emerging technology development.
* Flexibility & Remote Opportunities – Whether in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, we offer the technology and support to keep teams connected and productive.
* Career Stability & Growth – In this expanding industry, we invest in our people, providing opportunities & advancement in a stable, growing company.
* Generous Benefits Package - Switch provides comprehensive coverage for you and your family that can be tailored to fit your personal needs, and more!

### **Join Us & Make a Difference**

This is more than a job—it's a mission. If you're ready to be part of a culture that values innovation, karma, and limitless potential, we want to hear from you.

Apply Now and Let's Build the Future Together.

Your privacy rights may vary by location. Learn more in our Switch Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice https://www.switch.com/applicant-and-candidate-privacy/ to understand how Switch collects, uses, shares, and protects your personal information during the recruiting process.

**Safe Hiring Notice**  
Legitimate Switch recruiting emails come from switch.com. Current opportunities are posted on https://switch.com/careers and the official Switch LinkedIn Company page https://www.linkedin.com/company/switch-data-centers/. Switch also considers qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable law.

title: Senior Director, Product Creative Direction
description:
**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

**Team and Role**

This role is part of our Product Design team, which turns a deep understanding of our users and customers into product experiences they love. Our designers bring expertise across design systems, visual design, interaction design, content design, and product design. At ServiceNow, design has an intentional seat at the table, and we partner with Engineering and Product Management from the outset.

We're looking for a Senior Director of Product Creative Direction to define and evolve the visual expression of our product portfolio. This leader will set a distinctive product visual direction, translate it into a scalable system, and help teams make complex enterprise software feel clear, coherent, modern, and unmistakably ServiceNow.

This is a product-focused creative leadership role. You will work as part of cross-functional software development teams and partner across Platform and the business units to connect creative vision with customer needs, product strategy, and technical realities. Product teams retain ownership of their product strategy, design, roadmap, quality, and delivery; this role provides shared visual direction, systems, critique, and enablement.

You will also advance the responsible use of AI in creative work and make accessibility intrinsic to the product visual language.

**What you get to do in this role**

* Define and champion a differentiated visual direction for the product portfolio, grounded in our brand, customer needs, product strategy, and the evolving relationship between people and AI.
* Establish a clear point of view across typography, color, composition, iconography, illustration, motion, data visualization, density, and other visual foundations.
* Create future-state concepts, reference experiences, and exemplars that make the visual direction tangible.
* Work with Design Systems, Product Design, Content Design, Accessibility, Localization, and Research to translate the visual language into scalable foundations, components, patterns, and guidance.
* Partner with Design Systems, Product Management and Engineering throughout the software development lifecycle so the creative direction can be applied effectively in shipped products.
* Define where consistency is essential, where variation creates value, and how teams can extend the system without creating a centralized bottleneck.
* Lead the strategy for AI-enabled creative exploration, prototyping, asset creation, system evolution, and evaluation, focusing on meaningful gains in range, speed, consistency, and quality.
* Move promising AI approaches from experimentation to repeatable practice through pilots, playbooks, training, exemplars, responsible-use standards, and measurable adoption goals.
* Provide creative direction and hands-on critique for priority, cross-product initiatives while reinforcing product-team ownership.
* Partner with Brand and Marketing so the company expression and product experience tell a coherent story while remaining useful and native to interactive software.
* Make accessibility intrinsic to the creative vision and visual foundations, partnering with Accessibility and Engineering to meet or exceed applicable standards, including WCAG 2.2 AA.
* Lead, develop, and attract exceptional visual, motion, and multidisciplinary design talent.
* Build the culture, enablement, and shared critique practices that help product designers and distributed visual designers understand, apply, and continually raise the visual craft bar.
* Build a network of creative leaders and contributors across the business units who can extend the direction while maintaining coherence.

 **Qualifications**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 12+ years of experience in product design, visual design, experience design, creative direction, or a related field, including significant leadership experience shipping complex digital products.
* A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft and creative leadership across shipped product experiences, not only brand campaigns or marketing communications.
* Experience defining or materially evolving a visual language across a complex, multi-product software portfolio.
* Deep understanding of design systems, including visual foundations, design tokens, components, patterns, governance, contribution models, and the relationship between design and code.
* Demonstrated experience adopting AI-enabled creative tools and workflows and moving teams from isolated experimentation to sustained, responsible use at scale.
* Proven ability to influence senior executives and align multiple organizations without relying solely on reporting authority.
* Expert command of typography, color, composition, interaction, motion, and information hierarchy, with the judgment to apply them to dense and complex product workflows.
* Strong systems thinking and the ability to connect an inspiring creative idea to the practices and adoption mechanisms required to make it real at scale.
* Demonstrated commitment to accessible and inclusive design, with working knowledge of WCAG and platform accessibility considerations.
* Excellent communication, storytelling, facilitation, and critique skills, including the ability to make a direction compelling to executives and actionable for delivery teams.
* Experience leading leaders and building high-performing, inclusive creative teams.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Experience participating in the complete product development lifecycle of web and/or software applications.
* Experience working as a member of cross-functional Product Management, Engineering, and Design teams.
* Experience leading creative teams and partnering across a complex organization.

title: Director of Brand & Creative Marketing
description:
**Director of Brand & Creative Marketing**
==========================================

Marketing | Full-Time, Exempt | Reports to the Co-CEOs | Remote (U.S.) | Director: $150k-210k
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

***Please note: Must submit a portfolio to be considered for this role.***

**About the Role**
------------------

Seeking is looking for a highly entrepreneurial, hands-on **Director / Sr. Director of Brand & Creative Marketing** to lead the brand side of our marketing organization.

This is not a traditional management role and it is not a position for someone who wants to sit above the work.

We are looking for an operator.

This person will own Seeking's brand marketing strategy and lead an approximately 13-person organization spanning PR, creative, copy, social, influencer marketing, and broader brand initiatives and activations. They will be responsible for turning company goals into marketing strategy, turning strategy into executable plans, ensuring the right people are accountable for the right work, and ultimately determining whether that work is moving the business.

The role works closely with Seeking's Co-CEOs and alongside our Director of Growth and Lifecycle Marketing. Our Digital Marketing team owns areas such as paid acquisition, lifecycle/CRM, conversion optimization, and digital growth. This role owns the brand side of marketing while partnering closely with Growth to ensure both functions operate as one marketing organization and share accountability for company performance.

Seeking moves quickly. Our team is lean, scrappy, ambitious, and highly adaptable. The right person is comfortable making decisions, changing direction when the data requires it, getting into the details, and personally helping solve problems when necessary.

We do not need another layer of management. We need someone capable of building and leading a high-performing marketing organization.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

### **Marketing strategy, performance, and budget**

* Own Seeking's brand marketing strategy, positioning, messaging, audience strategy, and overall brand direction.
* Translate company objectives into quarterly and annual marketing priorities, initiatives, OKRs, budgets, and measurable business outcomes.
* Develop the marketing strategy in close partnership with the Co-CEOs, progressively assuming greater ownership as alignment and trust are established.
* Understand Seeking's distinct audiences and develop strategies capable of effectively reaching both sides of the marketplace.
* Identify untapped audiences, market opportunities, positioning gaps, competitive opportunities, and new ways to grow the business.
* Own consumer research, competitive intelligence, campaign learnings, and brand insights.
* Determine what Seeking should do more of, less of, stop doing, or approach differently based on performance and business priorities.

### **Integrated Campaign Leadership**

* Originate and lead major brand campaigns from initial insight through strategy, concept, execution, launch, measurement, and post-campaign analysis.
* Develop bold, culturally relevant ideas capable of generating conversation, press, signups, and revenue.
* Define the objective, audience, strategic insight, messaging, channels, success metrics, budget, responsibilities, and execution plan for major initiatives.
* Work closely with Creative, Production, PR, Social, Influencer, Digital Marketing, Product, Legal, and external partners to bring campaigns to market.
* Personally contribute ideas rather than relying exclusively on the team for campaign concepts.
* Evaluate concepts, scripts, copy, messaging, creative direction, activations, partnerships, and channel plans with strong creative and commercial judgment.
* Lead campaign production, including talent, agencies, production partners, shoots, post-production, rollout, media requirements, legal considerations, and timelines.

### **Performance & Business Accountability**

* Own the performance of the brand marketing organization and ensure marketing activity ultimately contributes to business growth.
* Monitor company and marketing performance closely, including joins, revenue, CAC, ROAS, conversion, brand search, campaign performance, social growth, influencer performance, earned media, and other relevant KPIs.
* Diagnose why initiatives are or are not working and make changes quickly.
* Reallocate budget, resources, priorities, or strategy when performance does not justify the current approach.
* Maximize ROI across productions and activations by identifying opportunities to create additional revenue-driving content within existing budgets, helping recover costs and improve the overall return on each investment.
* Establish meaningful measurement frameworks for brand initiatives that connect marketing activity to commercial outcomes, including brand health.
* Partner closely with the Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing to understand acquisition and funnel performance and ensure brand and performance marketing strengthen one another.
* Lead campaign and quarterly retrospectives and turn learnings into concrete changes.

### **PR & Cultural Relevance**

* Set the overarching PR narrative and determine what Seeking should be known for culturally.
* Lead and challenge the PR organization on strategy, angles, pitches, media opportunities, reactive opportunities, partnerships, spokesperson positioning, and execution.
* Help develop provocative, differentiated stories that can break through crowded cultural conversations while protecting the business and brand.
* Be comfortable operating around controversial subjects and challenging cultural conversations without becoming unnecessarily risk-averse.
* Understand what makes a story interesting to media rather than simply what the company wants to communicate.
* Be capable of rewriting or strengthening an angle, headline, pitch, talking point, or narrative when senior intervention is required.
* Build and develop a strong internal PR function rather than relying exclusively on agencies to provide strategic thinking.
* Own reputation and crisis communications, partnering with the Co-CEOs and Legal to protect the brand.

### **Team Leadership & Organizational Performance**

* Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable an approximately 13-person brand marketing organization.
* Manage managers and senior individual contributors across Creative, Production, PR, Social, Influencer, Copy, Brand Marketing, and related functions.
* Establish clear ownership, expectations, goals, accountability, and decision-making authority across the department.
* Evaluate talent continuously and identify where employees need coaching, clearer expectations, additional resources, changed responsibilities, or stronger performance management.
* Recognize high-potential employees and create opportunities for them to grow.
* Make difficult personnel recommendations when performance does not meet the needs of the business.
* Identify organizational gaps and recommend changes to team structure, roles, hiring plans, agencies, contractors, or external resources.
* Participate meaningfully in recruiting, interviewing, hiring, performance management, and termination decisions.
* Build a culture that combines empathy and development with extremely high standards for performance.

### **Marketing Operations & Planning**

* Own the integrated marketing calendar in partnership with the Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing.
* Set department priorities and determine what gets worked on, delayed, re-scoped, or stopped.
* Turn large initiatives into clear workstreams, owners, milestones, dependencies, budgets, timelines, and success metrics.
* Build and continuously improve the operating processes required for a sophisticated marketing organization.
* Establish clear processes for briefs, campaign development, research, creative concepting, moodboards, reviews, approvals, production, PR planning, launch readiness, asset delivery, reporting, and postmortems.
* Ensure teams are brought into initiatives at the right stage rather than operating reactively.
* Remove bottlenecks before they reach the executive team.
* Identify unclear ownership and correct it.
* Ensure initiatives move forward without requiring the Co-CEOs to manage day-to-day execution.

### **Budget & Commercial Management**

* Own and manage a significant seven-figure brand marketing budget.
* Build annual and quarterly budgets and allocate resources against the highest-value opportunities.
* Evaluate spend based on strategic importance and expected business return.
* Maintain visibility into commitments, actual spend, forecasts, and ROI.
* Oversee agencies, production partners, talent, influencers, vendors, sponsorships, and other external relationships.
* Lead or oversee high-stakes negotiations and ensure the team is negotiating effectively.
* Challenge unnecessary spend and identify opportunities to achieve better outcomes with existing resources.

**How This Role Works With Other Marketing Leaders**
----------------------------------------------------

### **Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing**

The Director / Sr. Director of Brand & Creative Marketing and Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing will operate as peer leaders.

This role owns brand strategy, integrated brand campaigns, PR, Creative, Copy, Social, Influencer, brand activations, consumer insights, and the brand marketing budget.

The two leaders jointly plan around company goals, audience strategy, campaign performance, acquisition, landing-page effectiveness, creative performance, the marketing calendar, and overall business growth.

  

**Leadership vs. Delegation**
-----------------------------

The Director creates the environment in which the marketing team can perform at a higher level by setting the strategy, establishing priorities, structuring the work, challenging the thinking, coaching the team, reviewing performance, removing gaps, and holding the organization accountable for results.

At the same time, this is a hands-on leadership role.

When a major campaign needs a stronger concept, a pitch needs to be rewritten, messaging is not working, a brief is unclear, a negotiation is stuck, or an important initiative needs senior attention, this person is expected to get involved and help solve it.

Strong leaders here do not say, "That's not my job."

They also do not take over their employees' jobs.

They know when to coach, when to challenge, when to make the decision, and when to roll up their sleeves.

**What We Are Looking For**
---------------------------

* 8+ years of progressive marketing experience, with exceptional candidates considered based on demonstrated scope and trajectory rather than years alone.
* 4+ years of meaningful people-management experience, including experience managing managers or senior functional leaders.
* Demonstrated experience across both brand marketing and PR/communications.
* Strong experience developing and executing integrated consumer marketing campaigns.
* Experience in a startup, high-growth environment, agency environment, or similarly fast-moving business, with the ability to operate with a high sense of urgency and keep pace with rapid execution, shifting priorities, and tight deadlines.
* Experience owning or meaningfully managing substantial marketing budgets.
* Experience working with agencies, production companies, creators, talent, vendors, and external partners.
* Working knowledge of campaign production from concept through delivery and distribution.
* Exceptional copy judgment and the ability to provide meaningful feedback across advertising, PR, social, influencer scripts, campaign messaging, and brand communications.
* Strong negotiator with sound commercial judgment.
* Experience creating structure, processes, and accountability inside growing or evolving teams.
* Comfortable making difficult decisions with incomplete information.
* Able to operate effectively with founders and senior executives who are highly engaged in the brand.
* Confident enough to challenge an executive recommendation when the data, customer insight, or strategy supports a different direction.

Marketplace or two-sided consumer platform experience is a plus.

Experience with culturally provocative, unconventional, entertainment, lifestyle, dating, or otherwise conversation-driving brands is highly valued.

description:
Proof is the world's first identity-assured transaction management platform and we are on a mission to digitize trust for all of life’s most critical transactions. Developed by the same market leaders and experts who brought notarization online with Notarize℠, Proof offers trust in a digital world by verifying identities and securing transactions to protect businesses and their customers. Since 2015, we’ve completed many of the world’s first digital commerce transactions, including the first online real estate closing, online mortgage closing, online auto sale, and online will and we're still just getting started!

Proof's brand has to signal two things at once: the rigor of a WebTrust-audited certificate authority that banks can rely on, and the simplicity of an identity people can verify once and reuse anywhere. As Proof expands from the online notarization category we created into portable digital identity and agentic authorization, our brand needs to grow with us.

As Director of Brand and Creative, you'll own Proof's brand strategy, visual and verbal identity, and creative output across every touchpoint, including proof.com, campaigns, events, sales materials, and executive presence. Day to day, you'll set creative direction, lead design production, and build a brand that earns trust from regulated institutions and stands out in identity and fintech.

### **What you’ll do as the Director of Brand and Creative at Proof:**

* Brand strategy and architecture: Define and steward Proof's brand platform (purpose, personality, voice, and the promise of trust in high-consequence transactions), and develop brand architecture for the platform, VDC, notarization, and agentic authorization with the Director of Product Marketing. Lead brand evolution or refresh work as needed.
* Visual and verbal identity: Own the brand system and guidelines, including logo, color, typography, iconography, illustration, photography, motion, and data visualization. Partner with the Head of Demand Content and Director of Communications on tone-of-voice guidelines.
* Brand hub and templates: Build a self-serve brand hub and template library so Sales,  
  Marketing, and the wider company stay on brand.
* Campaign and launch creative: Lead creative concepting and execution for  
  campaigns, product launches, and brand moments with Revenue Marketing and Product Marketing.
* Design across touchpoints: Oversee design for proof.com, digital advertising, sales collateral, presentations, video, social, and event environments, including booth and experiential design with the Event Marketing Manager.
* Creative operations: Run intake, prioritization, and review and approval workflows, and manage creative budgets, agencies, and freelancers.
* Brand health and governance: Establish brand health metrics and research  
  (awareness, consideration, perception among target buyers), govern consistency across marketing, sales, partners, and co-marketing, and work with Product Design so the product and marketing brand feel like one company.

### **What we're looking for:**

* 10+ years in brand and creative, including 4+ years leading brand or creative teams at a B2B technology, fintech, or security company, or senior agency experience on comparable brands.
* A portfolio showing brand systems and campaigns that made complex or trust-centric products clear and distinctive.
* Experience leading a brand refresh or new brand architecture during a company's category expansion.
* Strong creative direction across design, copy, video, and motion, and the ability to get hands-on when needed.
* Ability to align executives on creative decisions and explain the business rationale behind brand choices.

### **You'll really stand out if you have:**

* Experience building brands for financial services, payments, or identity companies.
* Experience with AI-assisted creative workflows and modern tooling (Figma, Adobe CC, Webflow).
* Experience spanning both B2B enterprise and consumer-facing touchpoints.

**Travel:** This role will include occasional travel for Proof Summit, team onsites, industry events, and customer or partner meetings. Your manager will share more about expected travel during the interview process.

* **Pave the Way:** When obstacles arise, we break through barriers with passion and perseverance. We lead with creativity and forward-thinking. We aim to set new standards and shape the future in a repeatable, scalable way so the path to success is easier for our team to follow.
* **Own It:** We embrace the responsibility that comes with supporting life's most important transactions. When a problem arises we relentlessly pursue the solution with a 'Yes before no' attitude. Because every problem and every transaction is treated like it's our own.
* **Act with Integrity:** We are in the business of building trust and it is at the core of everything we do. We are honest and transparent with our customers, each other and ourselves. If we make a mistake, we own up to it right away and do what it takes to make it right. Our dedication to security and compliance is key to earning trust, fighting fraud and ultimately, our success.
* **Play to Win:** We believe excellence is about always striving to be better so when we get it wrong, we iterate, we learn and we grow. We know we can only go so far alone, we're better together and collectively, we win!

**About Ancestry:**

When you join Ancestry, you join a human-centered company where every person’s story is important. Ancestry®, the global leader in family history, connects everyone with their past so they can discover, preserve, and share their unique family stories. With our unparalleled collection of more than 65 billion records, over 3.5 million subscribers, and over 27 million people in our growing DNA network, customers can discover their family story and gain a new level of understanding about their lives. Over the past 40 years, we’ve built trusted relationships with millions of people who have chosen us as the platform for discovering, preserving, and sharing the most important information about themselves and their families.
  
  
We are committed to our location flexible work approach, allowing you to choose to work in the nearest office, from your home, or a hybrid of both (subject to location restrictions and roles that are required to be in the office- ). We will continue to hire and promote beyond the boundaries of our office locations, to enable broadened possibilities for employee diversity.
  
  
Together, we work every day to foster a work environment that's inclusive as well as diverse, and where our people can be themselves. Every idea and perspective is valued so that our products and services reflect the global and diverse clients we serve.
  
  
Ancestry encourages applications from minorities, women, the disabled, protected veterans and all other qualified applicants. Passionate about dedicating your work to enriching people’s lives? Join the curious.

This role is a rare opportunity to lead design for the heart of Ancestry’s product—the Tree, the Person Page, Merge, and Records—foundational experiences that define how millions of users engage with their family history. As Director of Product Design on the Engage team, you’ll be at the center of our most critical product surfaces, ensuring they work seamlessly together to deliver clarity, connection, and discovery. This is not just about optimizing what already exists; it’s about reimagining how these core experiences evolve as a unified ecosystem. It requires a design leader with a strong product sensibility, a systems-thinking mindset, and the ability to balance craft with scale. You’ll need to advocate across disciplines, align with senior stakeholders, and guide a team through complexity and legacy to deliver elegant, human-centered solutions. For someone who wants to shape the future of our flagship experience—and the legacy of the Ancestry brand—this is that moment.

  

**What you’ll do**

* Lead the design vision and execution for the Engage team, ensuring cohesion and delight across the full customer journey.
* Partner across product areas and functions to eliminate friction, fill gaps, and ensure customers experience Ancestry as a rich, connected, and purpose-driven platform.
* Identify and prioritize key moments in the user journey that drive trust, retention, and discovery — and improve them through thoughtful product design and iteration.
* Collaborate closely with product, engineering, data, marketing, and customer support to ensure every touchpoint is aligned and intentional.
* Translate insights from qualitative research and quantitative data into actionable design direction, balancing creativity and clarity.
* Evangelize the customer journey internally — bringing a user-first lens to cross-org decision making and fostering a culture of customer empathy.
* Guide the creation of key design artifacts, including user flows, prototypes, wireframes, and visual systems.
* Coach and mentor a team of talented designers, helping them collaborate and grow as strategic thinkers and empathic customer advocates.

**Who you are**

* Extensive experience in UX or product design, including a track record of leading design in cross-functional, collaborative environments.
* Proven ability to move between strategic thinking and hands-on execution with ease.
* Deep understanding of end-to-end customer journey mapping and experience design.
* Experience leading teams focused on onboarding, lifecycle, navigation, and engagement.
* A strong foundation in human-centered design, with the ability to bring clarity to complex or unfamiliar spaces.
* Strong communicator and influencer who can align diverse stakeholders around a shared vision.
* Passionate about creating connected, high-trust experiences that put the user first.
* *Bonus: Background in consumer subscription products, digital ecosystems, or identity-driven experiences.*

  

**Why Ancestry?**

Join a dedicated team working to connect millions of people with their past and enrich their futures. At Ancestry, you will play a role in pioneering legal solutions that shape the consumer genomics industry. Your contributions will help foster and protect our workforce that is dedicated to helping our customers tell their own stories, while supporting a brand recognized and trusted around the world. We offer a collaborative workplace, competitive compensation, and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference.

Ancestry values pay transparency and equity. Director of Employer Engagement and Career Design

  

**Posting Number:**

WPU0065317

Center for Student Success

Full Time (12-Months, On-Site with occassional remote work opportunities)

10/10/2026

10/25/2026

title: Director of Design
description:
About Mendocino Farms
  
At Mendocino Farms, we do a lot more than just sell sandwiches and salads. We are a fast-casual restaurant brand on a mission to bring people together through fresh, culinary-driven food and unmatched hospitality. As we continue our aggressive growth trajectory across new and existing markets, we are seeking a dynamic, analytical, and hands-on leader to elevate our total rewards structure.
  
Our Core Values and Mantras
  

* Sell Happy: The foundational philosophy that goes beyond serving meals to actively uplifting and improving every guest's day.
* Food Should Make People Feel Good: A commitment to using high-quality, whole, and thoughtfully sourced ingredients that make eating well easy.
* Be Culinary Explorers: A passion for combining fresh ingredients and bold flavors in unexpected, gourmet ways.
* Turn the Ordinary into the Extraordinary: Treating every customer and team interaction as a chance to lift someone's spirits.
* Get Better Every Day (GBED): An internal mantra encouraging continuous learning, personal growth, and skill development.

Director of Design
  
  
**Reports To:** VP, Design & Construction
  
**FLSA Status:** Exempt
  
**Cost Center:** 9511
  
**Location:** Dallas, TX or Remote, USA
  
**Salary Range:** $117,000–$190,000 (Compensation is based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.)
  
  
Position Summary
  
Mendocino Farms is seeking a Director of Design to lead the evolution and delivery of our restaurant experience across new restaurants, remodels, refreshes, and strategic initiatives.
  
**This leader will own Mendo’s design function:** the restaurant prototype, design standards, internal and external design resources, and the systems that turn brand strategy into distinctive, functional, and scalable restaurants. You will partner closely with Operations, Culinary, Facilities, Construction, Real Estate, and Marketing to create environments that strengthen the guest experience while supporting efficient operations, disciplined investment, and growth.
  
This is an opportunity for a creative and operationally minded leader who can set a compelling design point of view, build a high-performing team and consultant network, and make practical decisions that balance quality, durability, speed, cost, and long-term unit performance as Mendocino Farms expands its restaurant footprint.
  
Core Responsibilities
  
Lead the Design Function
  

* Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop internal designers and external design resources; set clear expectations, effective working rhythms, and a high bar for quality and accountability.
* Resource Alignment: Align internal and external design resources to the development pipeline, identifying when specialized expertise is needed.
* Senior Design Leadership: Serve as the senior design leader for complex, high-visibility, or high-risk projects and decisions.

Own the Brand Environment and Design Standards
  

* Prototype & Standards Ownership: Own and evolve Mendo’s restaurant prototype, design standards, material palettes, finishes, furniture, fixtures, lighting, equipment integration, and reusable design details.

* Cross-Functional Partnership: Creates alignment across Operations, Culinary, Facilities, Construction, Real Estate, Marketing, and vendors.

* Continuous Improvement: Uses field learning, post-project reviews, and market insight to strengthen standards and systems.
* Clear Decision-Making: Communicates concise recommendations, surfaces risks and tradeoffs, and documents follow-through.

Qualifications, Education & Experience
  
  
**Required:**  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Interior Architecture, Interior Design, Environmental Design, Product Design, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in restaurant, retail, hospitality, architecture, interior design, or another related built-environment discipline.
* Leadership: Experience leading a design team, studio, function, or substantial network of external design partners in a fast-moving, multi-project environment.
* Industry Footprint: Significant hands-on experience with restaurant or similarly operationally intensive commercial design, including prototype development, new-unit growth, remodels, and site-specific adaptation.
* Operational Design: Strong command of FOH/BOH flow, kitchen equipment, labor and ergonomics, guest circulation and accessibility, pickup and delivery, food safety, storage, and maintainability.
* Partner Management: Experience managing architects, interior designers, engineers, and specialty vendors against quality, schedule, scope, and budget expectations.

* Financial Acumen: Fluency with design budgets, cost drivers, value engineering, specification tradeoffs, lifecycle durability, and unit economics.
* Communication: Exceptional written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including concise recommendations and executive-ready presentations.
* Travel: Ability to travel occasionally for market visits, project milestones, and team meetings.

**Preferred:**

title: Director of Learning Design
description:
**About Tergar Schools**

Tergar Schools is a Buddhist-inspired K–12 education nonprofit building a new model of learning (MOL). We operate a pilot school in Kathmandu, Nepal, and are constructing a larger campus in the Yolmo Valley in the Himalayas.

Our model rests on a simple starting point: every child possesses basic goodness and its qualities of awareness, love, compassion, wisdom, and joy. It is our job as educators to help them recognize this and give them tools to sustain it. Our long-term aspiration is to help form people who are resilient, altruistic, and joyful.

We’re now building the next chapter of that work: a comprehensive, fully secular model designed to weave into any school’s existing life — not just our own campuses. Rather than build more schools ourselves, we intend to reach 100+ schools in 4+ countries within five years by helping other schools, secular or religious, adopt the model as their own.

**Why This Role Exists**

Our footprint is growing quickly. Two high-performing private schools will begin piloting our model of learning in 2027. A research lab opens in Nepal with a world-class science team. The interest is real and growing.

What we don’t have yet is a full-time position for building the model itself — the products, courses, training materials, and classroom materials that will constitute MOL — and for leading the team that builds it out.

Today that thinking lives mostly with our Executive Director and the instincts of our founding team. This isn’t sustainable at scale. We need someone who can be fully dedicated to this element of our project: an outside-the-box thinker with real contemplative experience, genuinely excited by the challenge of building an entire family of products from scratch rather than adapting an existing portfolio.

**The Opportunity**

This is a builder’s role. You will not inherit a finished product, a proven training program, or a team. You will build those things — starting hands-on, in the room, with our first two outside partner schools — and then lead the team that takes them to scale.

We have materials. However, none of them is a comprehensive, fully secular contemplative model designed to weave into everything a school already does. That is what you would be building, and there is no template for it.

If you are energized by deciding who you need around you rather than inheriting an org chart, and comfortable being personally in the work now so that later you can hand it to people you have trained this is the position for you. .

**What You’ll Own**

**Building the model**

* Design the teacher training program at the center of the MOL — the core product.
* Build out the materials that make the training usable in a real school. Today we imagine adaptable toolkits fitted by hand to each school, a playbook for staff and administrators, and family-facing materials. That is a starting hypothesis, not a spec — the process of choosing what comes is yours to lead.
* Run the model as a product, not a document. Form real hypotheses about what teachers and schools need, test them in live classrooms, and let what you learn change what gets built.
* Propose what gets built now and what waits — and defend those calls. We hold two commitments at once: build lean, and be the best in the world at this. We call it *Minimum Viable Mastery*. You are the person who makes that real week to week, not just in principle.

**Nailing the first schools**

* Be personally hands-on with our new partner schools in Nepal as they begin onboarding in 2027. You will do this work in tandem with the Executive Director (ED).
* Use what you learn there to define what a stable first phase actually looks like, and build the real template other schools will follow.

**Building your team**

* Decide what team you need, and in what order — a Nepal Country Director and Trainer, Country Coordinators, strategic consultants, instructional designers, a UX researcher, and others as the shape of the work becomes clear (a Head of Training in Nepal is currently being hired).
* The ED and the Director of Operations (DOO) authorize and execute the actual hiring. The judgment about who and when is yours.

**Setting the standard, over time**

* Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and the ED hold final say on model fidelity today. As you build a track record — likely marked by a completed first onboarding cycle with our two partner schools — that authority shifts substantively to you.
* Turn Rinpoche’s two to four multi-day sessions a year into material the team can use again: recorded, distilled, built into training, rather than a remarkable conversation nobody can revisit.

**Working with the evidence**

* Partner with the research lab opening in Nepal in late 2026 — led by Drs. Richard Davidson, Robert Roeser, and Robin Nusslock — translating what they learn into real product and training decisions.

  

**What’s Yours, and What Isn’t**

You own the model and the team you build around you. Three things sit outside that:

* **Fundraising and donor relationships.** A separate role entirely.
* **In-country adaptation and community relationships.** Local teams own this on the ground, but you liaise with them directly and are in very frequent communication.
* **Hiring mechanics.** You decide who you need and when; the DOO handles offers, contracts, and process.

One thing sits in between: **production**. Instructional designers, visual designers, and media support will eventually build finished materials from your direction. You will not be making them yourself for long — but their quality is still on you.

**Who You Are**

**What we’re really looking for**

* **A builder grounded in pedagogy.** Deep pedagogical expertise is essential — you understand how children and adults actually learn, and you've designed for it. What sets you apart is that you build and deliver: you've turned that expertise into programs, curricula, or training that real teachers use. A tech or startup background alongside that is a genuine asset.
* **Fluency in a lean approach to product design.** You can talk concretely about strategic experiments, problem/solution and product/market fit, and validated learning — and you have actually worked that way, not just read about it.
* **Real, lived contemplative experience.** A genuine taste of practice, not necessarily in Tergar’s own lineage, and not merely theoretical familiarity. This is the one non-negotiable that doesn’t bend for the right resume.
* **Comfortable being hands-on first and stepping back later.** Personally in the work with our first schools, then deliberately building the standards and training that let a team carry it without you in the room.
* **Able to build lean and aim to be the best in the world at the same time,** without treating those as a trade-off.

**Experience**

* You bring substantial experience in education — as a teacher, school leader, curriculum developer, or learning designer — and you've built something real from that experience and gotten it into people's hands without much money or staff.
* Some experience directing, mentoring, or building a team from scratch, since you will be doing exactly that here.
* Comfort working directly from a founder’s evolving vision rather than a finished brief — you will be co-writing the brief as you go, especially in the first months.

**Personal qualities**

* Discernment above all: knowing which calls are yours to make outright and which need to go to the Rinpoche or the ED. This carries more weight here than almost any other quality, because for a long stretch there is no layer of management between your judgment and the model’s integrity.
* Genuine curiosity about and respect for a tradition that may not be your own, without needing to adopt it as your own practice.
* Comfortable with ambiguity and a mandate that will keep changing shape under you as the first schools teach you things no one currently knows.

  

**How We Work Together**

* Intensive, hands-on time in Nepal during onboarding and the first deployment of the model. Expect three to five months during the first year.
* Frequent, close contact with the ED for the first six months, settling into a slower rhythm as trust builds.
* Two to four multi-day sessions a year with Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche, alongside the wider team.
* A small, distributed, high-autonomy culture across Vermont, Wisconsin, Ireland, Kathmandu, and Minnesota — deep, steady, skillful work over speed.

  

**Compensation & Logistics**

* Full-time
* Fully remote.
* Compensation: $75,000–$100,000, DOE
* Benefits: flexible schedule, unlimited PTO, and health care reimbursement up to $1,000 per month

title: Director of Marketing
description:
CyberSheath Services International LLC is a rapidly growing Managed Services Provider primarily focused on providing Cybersecurity services to the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). We are excited to be expanding our staff due to our growth and are looking to add a Director of Channel Partnerships & Business Development to our team!

CyberSheath integrates compliance and threat mitigation efforts and eliminates redundant security practices that don't improve and, in fact, may weaken an organization's security posture. Our professionals tell clients where to stop spending, where to invest, and how to take what they are already doing and integrate it in a way that delivers improved security.

Successful candidates for CyberSheath are self-motivated, think out of the box, work, and solve issues independently. Additionally, our most successful people are self-starters and willing to put on many hats in order to succeed. CyberSheath is fast-growing and seeks candidates who want to be part of our upward trajectory.

Position Overview

CyberSheath is seeking a strategic, hands-on Director of Marketing to build and lead a high-performing marketing function during a pivotal period of market growth and increasing CMMC adoption. This leader will own the development and execution of an integrated marketing strategy that strengthens brand authority, creates qualified pipeline, accelerates revenue, and positions CyberSheath as the trusted cybersecurity compliance partner for the Defense Industrial Base.

The Director of Marketing will translate complex cybersecurity, regulatory, and technical concepts into clear, credible, audience-specific messaging that resonates with executive buyers, IT and security leaders, compliance stakeholders, and operational leaders at defense contractors. This person will combine strategic rigor with operational excellence—setting the go-to-market plan while remaining close to campaigns, content, events, demand generation, performance analytics, and sales alignment.

The ideal candidate is a data-driven B2B marketing leader with experience in cybersecurity, managed services, compliance technology, government contracting, or similarly complex technical markets. They are comfortable operating in a growth-stage, private equity-backed environment, understand long sales cycles and multi-stakeholder buying committees, and know how to create measurable marketing impact.

What You'll Do

Marketing Strategy and Go-to-Market

* Develop and lead CyberSheath's annual and quarterly marketing strategy in partnership with executive leadership, sales, solution engineering, customer success, and service delivery.
* Define target segments, ideal customer profiles, buyer personas, market priorities, and account-tiering strategies for defense contractors and subcontractors navigating CMMC, DFARS, and NIST SP 800-171 requirements.
* Build integrated go-to-market plans for CyberSheath's core managed compliance, managed security, managed IT, assessment, implementation, and secure enclave offerings.
* Establish clear marketing priorities, budgets, milestones, operating cadences, and performance expectations tied to company revenue objectives.
* Identify market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and customer pain points that should inform messaging, campaigns, sales enablement, and product/service positioning.
* Support market expansion and new-service launches with disciplined positioning, audience targeting, launch planning, campaign execution, and performance measurement.

Demand Generation and Revenue Marketing

* Own the demand-generation engine from awareness through opportunity creation, working closely with Sales to drive pipeline quality, velocity, conversion, and revenue contribution.
* Create and optimize multi-channel campaigns across digital advertising, search, email nurture, webinars, content syndication, events, partner marketing, social media, and account-based marketing.
* Design programs that engage key buying-committee members, including CEOs, COOs, CFOs, CISOs, CIOs, IT leaders, compliance leaders, program managers, and operations executives.
* Partner with Sales leadership to define lead stages, service-level agreements, qualification criteria, routing processes, follow-up expectations, and closed-loop reporting.
* Build account-based marketing programs for priority accounts, strategic verticals, and high-value partner ecosystems.
* Develop nurture paths that educate prospective customers on compliance urgency, business risk, assessment readiness, remediation needs, and the operational requirements of maintaining CMMC compliance over time.
* Continuously test audience, channel, message, offer, and conversion-path hypotheses to improve marketing efficiency and pipeline outcomes.

Brand, Messaging, and Content

* Own CyberSheath's brand strategy, voice, positioning, messaging architecture, and narrative across external and internal-facing marketing assets.
* Ensure CyberSheath clearly communicates its differentiation as a specialized, end-to-end cybersecurity compliance partner for defense contractors rather than a generalist technology or security provider.
* Lead development of high-value thought leadership, including executive articles, regulatory explainers, blogs, guides, case studies, solution briefs, webinars, customer stories, analyst-facing content, and event presentations.
* Translate highly technical and regulatory subject matter into accessible, commercially relevant content without sacrificing accuracy or credibility.
* Partner with internal subject-matter experts to develop compelling perspectives on CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, secure CUI environments, managed security, assessment readiness, and continuous compliance.
* Maintain a high editorial standard and a consistent content calendar that supports organic demand, customer education, sales enablement, search visibility, and executive thought leadership.
* Oversee website messaging, conversion paths, content governance, SEO priorities, and user experience improvements.

Product and Sales Enablement

* Partner with Sales, Solution Engineering, and Service Delivery to sharpen service positioning, customer value propositions, competitive differentiation, and proof points.
* Develop sales-enablement materials such as pitch decks, battlecards, solution briefs, case studies, industry-specific messaging, objection-handling resources, and customer presentation templates.
* Equip revenue teams with clear, current, and consistent messaging for every stage of the buyer journey.
* Create mechanisms to capture and distribute market intelligence from prospects, customers, partners, competitors, and frontline revenue teams.
* Support customer marketing initiatives, including advocacy, testimonials, referral programs, case studies, and expansion campaigns.

Events, Partnerships, and Field Marketing

* Refine CyberSheath's strategy for industry events, trade shows, conferences, webinars, and executive programs relevant to the DIB, defense contracting, cybersecurity, compliance, and government technology markets.
* Ensure events are planned against measurable objectives, including target-account engagement, meeting generation, pipeline influence, partner activation, and revenue impact.
* Build co-marketing programs with strategic technology, channel, and ecosystem partners, including Microsoft and other organizations serving the compliance and defense-contractor market.
* Identify opportunities for CyberSheath executives and subject-matter experts to build visibility through speaking engagements, contributed content, media opportunities, and industry participation.

Analytics, Operations, and Team Leadership

* Establish a metrics-driven marketing operating model that measures awareness, engagement, marketing-sourced pipeline, marketing-influenced pipeline, conversion rates, customer acquisition cost, campaign ROI, pipeline velocity, and revenue contribution.
* Build and maintain reliable dashboards and executive reporting that clearly communicate marketing performance, key insights, risks, and recommended actions.
* Manage marketing technology, data hygiene, attribution, campaign operations, and budget discipline in partnership with Revenue Operations and other internal stakeholders.
* Evaluate and optimize the marketing technology stack, vendors, agencies, freelancers, and internal resources to ensure efficient execution.
* Hire, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing marketing team as the organization grows.
* Foster a collaborative, accountable, customer-centric culture that values speed, quality, experimentation, commercial impact, and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 6 to 12 months, the Director of Marketing will be expected to:

* Establish a clear, differentiated, and consistent market narrative for CyberSheath and its service portfolio.
* Implement an integrated demand-generation strategy that produces a predictable flow of qualified opportunities.
* Strengthen alignment between Marketing, Sales, Solution Engineering, and Customer Success around target accounts, lead management, messaging, and pipeline goals.
* Improve visibility into marketing performance through practical, trusted funnel and revenue reporting.
* Elevate CyberSheath's thought-leadership presence in the CMMC, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, and broader DIB cybersecurity compliance market.
* Build a scalable content engine that supports organic growth, outbound sales efforts, customer education, and partner engagement.
* Improve conversion across core marketing journeys, including website engagement, webinar registration, gated-content conversion, demo requests, assessment inquiries, and sales-accepted leads.
* Establish a repeatable field, event, and partner-marketing framework tied to measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, communications, or a related field; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* 8+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience, including 3+ years in a marketing leadership role.
* Demonstrated success developing and executing marketing strategies that drive measurable pipeline, revenue, and market growth.
* Experience marketing complex B2B services, technology solutions, cybersecurity offerings, managed services, compliance solutions, SaaS, or enterprise IT services.
* Strong command of demand generation, account-based marketing, content strategy, digital marketing, field marketing, campaign operations, and marketing analytics.
* Experience supporting sales organizations with long, complex sales cycles and multiple economic, technical, and operational stakeholders.
* Proven ability to translate technical concepts into customer-focused positioning, messaging, and content.
* Strong executive communication, presentation, writing, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Experience managing budgets, agencies, vendors, and marketing technology platforms.
* Track record of building and leading high-performing teams in fast-moving, growth-oriented environments.
* Analytical mindset and fluency with funnel metrics, attribution, conversion analysis, pipeline reporting, and campaign performance optimization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in cybersecurity, cybersecurity compliance, managed security services, managed IT services, GRC, risk management, or regulated technology markets.
* Familiarity with the Defense Industrial Base, federal contracting, CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, FedRAMP, CUI, or government cloud environments.
* Experience marketing to defense contractors, manufacturers, engineering firms, federal contractors, or regulated mid-market organizations.
* Experience working in a private equity-backed or high-growth business environment.
* Familiarity with CRM, marketing automation, web analytics, SEO, paid media, intent-data, ABM, and attribution tools.
* Experience launching services, entering new markets, repositioning a brand, or scaling a marketing organization.

Work Environment

* Fully remote role with occasional travel for industry events and offsite meetings

*CyberSheath is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with a disability.*

title: Director of Brand
description:
**About this role**
-------------------

Boulder Care is hiring its first Director of Brand to own how trust is built with the people and communities we serve. You will lead the brand, content and creative system that makes Boulder's promise clear and credible, from our digital positioning and patient stories to campaigns, social, community partnerships and the materials that help people choose care.

This is a builder role. You will have the opportunity to create and mature a brand machine. You will turn a new messaging platform and visual refresh into a working system, lead a team and trusted external partners, and build a clear brand investment strategy with learning loops. You will report to the Chief Growth Officer and partner closely with Communications, Product, Clinical, and Commercial leadership.

Boulder Care is an award-winning digital clinic for addiction medicine, recognized for both innovation and high-quality patient care. Founded in 2017 by CEO Stephanie Strong, our mission is to improve the lives of people with substance use disorders through compassionate, evidence-based care.

We provide Boulder patients with a fully virtual, multidisciplinary care team, including medical providers and peer recovery specialists, who deliver personalized treatment, such as medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) and ongoing support. Our approach is grounded in clinical excellence, patient-centered care, and a commitment to reducing barriers to recovery. Boulder partners with leading health plans, employers, and community organizations to ensure that our services are accessible and covered for the people who need them most.

Named by Fortune as one of the Best Workplaces in Healthcare, we foster a culture of kindness, respect, and meaningful work that delivers outstanding patient outcomes and moves the addiction medicine industry forward.

* Run Boulder's brand portfolio with a thesis, activation plan, budget discipline, measurement approach and renewal gate for every material investment.
* Translate a visual identity and messaging guide into an easy-to-use creative system: templates, channel guidance, campaign frameworks, art direction, and self-service guardrails.

**Work environment**
--------------------

* This is a full-time, 100% remote position. Availability during standard business hours is expected, with flexibility to support business needs.
* Travel up to 15% is expected for team gatherings, production, partnership activations and key company events.

* Office requirements: Boulder teammates working with sensitive information must have a dedicated, private workspace with a lockable door and high-speed internet to maintain a secure, distraction-free environment, ensuring compliance with HIPAA and confidentiality standards.
* Boulder Care employees are free to use our riverfront HQ located in Portland, OR, whenever they would like.

**Compensation**
----------------

The starting pay range for this position is **$175,000–$190,000**; base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave).

**Perks and benefits**
----------------------

* Mental health services via insurance coverage, including Talkspace and EAP for continuous care
* 4 weeks of vacation accrued per calendar year with a tenured increase to 5 weeks at 2 years of employment

**Our values**

* Our opportunity is also our duty

* Turn bold ideas into even bolder action
* Strong individuals, stronger together
* Boulder Care recognizes the value that **lived experience** can provide to our organization, community, and patients. Applicants with lived experience and/or training as a peer recovery specialist are encouraged to apply.

We celebrate differences and are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or veteran status. **About Designs for Health**  
Designs for Health is a trusted leader in the nutraceutical industry, known for delivering high-quality, research-driven nutritional products that support better health outcomes.
